item.title: Reckoning and Renewing: Voices Along the Way
item.itunes:title: Reckoning and Renewing: Voices Along the Way
item.itunes:author: Janice Osborn and Rob Marus
item.description:
Part of the Reckoning and Renewing journey, FBC members Rob Marus and Janice Osborn offer the sermon. Their theme is "What I Inherited," a return to the question the series began with. What did your family hand you, spoken or unspoken, about race, difference, or who belongs? They share what they've set down, what they've kept on purpose, and what they hope to pass along.
00:00:00 Janice Osborn 00:08:15 This Little Light of Mine 00:09:16 Rob Marus
Readings: Psalm 121; 2 Corinthians 5:16-20; Matthew 5:1-16.
Watch the full worship service: https://www.firstbaptistdc.org/listen-to-sermons/2026/10/14/sunday-oct-18-2026-reckoning-and-renewing-voices-along-the-way
Sunday, October 18, 2026 · The First Baptist Church of the City of Washington, D.C.

item.title: Reckoning and Renewing: Which Jesus?
item.itunes:title: Reckoning and Renewing: Which Jesus?
item.itunes:author: Julie Pennington-Russell
item.description:
First Baptist continues our five-week series, Reckoning and Renewing, a chance to look honestly at our own story and our nation's, the dark pieces along with the redeeming ones. Pastor Julie preaches "Which Jesus?" from Matthew 16:13-20, where Jesus asks his disciples, "Who do you say that I am?"
For two thousand years, Christians have answered that question in ways that have shaped the world—sometimes toward peace and justice, sometimes toward conquest and slavery—with Scripture quoted in defense. What do we do with the truth that white supremacy in this nation was sustained, in large part, by the misuse of the Bible, in the name of the Savior to whom we belong?
Readings: Genesis 9:20-27; Romans 12:1-3; Matthew 16:13-20.
Watch the full worship service: https://www.firstbaptistdc.org/listen-to-sermons/2026/10/8/sunday-oct-11-2026-reckoning-and-renewing-which-jesus
Sunday, October 11, 2026 · The First Baptist Church of the City of Washington, D.C.

item.title: Reckoning and Renewing: Midnight in America
item.itunes:title: Reckoning and Renewing: Midnight in America
item.itunes:author: Rev. Kevin Peterman
item.description:
First Baptist's five-week series, Reckoning and Renewing, is a chance to look honestly at our own story and our nation's, the dark pieces along with the redeeming ones. When we can name what's true about the past without flinching, that past loses its power to hold us in regret or shame. The series moves us a step further into freedom: naming what we've inherited, wrestling with how scripture itself has been used and misused, listening to our own members' stories, and finally asking what faithfulness looks like as we walk forward together.
Rev. Kevin Peterman preaches "Midnight in America," from Acts 16:16-40, the story of Paul and Silas in jail.
Readings: Isaiah 58:6-9a; Acts 16:16-40; Matthew 23:1-7, 23-28.
Watch the full worship service: https://www.firstbaptistdc.org/listen-to-sermons/2026/10/4/sunday-oct-4-2026-midnight-in-america-rev-kevin-peterman
Sunday, October 4, 2026 · The First Baptist Church of the City of Washington, D.C.

item.title: Still Here When Mercy Offends
item.itunes:title: Still Here When Mercy Offends
item.itunes:author: Eric Mathis
item.description:
Pastor Eric wraps up the sermon series, Still Here: When Holding On Is Holy Enough, a four-week journey through the Hebrew Bible with people who had reached the end of themselves. The sermon immerses us in the story of Jonah.
In this passage, we sit with a prophet who is furious — not because God was harsh, but because God was merciful to the "wrong people." It's a story about what happens when grace reaches past the line we would have drawn, and whether we can bear it. The sermon holds that question, and carries it toward the work of reckoning and renewing.
Readings: Jonah 3:10-4:11; Psalm 145:1-8; Philippians 1:21-30; Matthew 20:1-16.
Watch the full worship service: https://www.firstbaptistdc.org/listen-to-sermons/2026/9/18/sunday-sep-20-2026-still-here-when-mercy-offends

item.title: Still Here When the Wound Is Old
item.itunes:title: Still Here When the Wound Is Old
item.itunes:author: Eric Mathis
item.description:
Pastor Eric continues the sermon series, Still Here: When Holding On Is Holy Enough, a four-week journey through the Hebrew Bible with people who had reached the end of themselves. The sermon revisits the story of Joseph.
In Genesis 50, Joseph's brothers are terrified now that their father has died, and expect the revenge they have earned. Instead, Joseph weeps and says to them, "You intended to do harm to me, but God intended it for good."
For anyone carrying an old wound that has not fully closed, this is not the false comfort of "everything happens for a reason." It is something more sturdy: permission to name the harm, grieve its reality, and set down the exhausting work of keeping score.
Readings: Genesis 50:15-21; Psalm 103:(1-7), 8-13; Romans 14:1-12; Matthew 18:21-35.
Watch the full worship service: https://www.firstbaptistdc.org/listen-to-sermons/2026/9/10/sunday-sep-13-2026-still-here-when-the-wound-is-old

item.title: Still Here When It’s Too Much
item.itunes:title: Still Here When It’s Too Much
item.itunes:author: Eric Mathis
item.description:
In this passage, Pastor Eric continues the sermon series, Still Here: When Holding On is Holy Enough, a four-week journey through the Hebrew Bible with people who had reached the end of themselves. Earlier in the series the journey sits with Jeremiah's burn out and honest complaint. Here the sermon meets Ezekiel, handed a responsibility almost too heavy to carry.
God appoints Ezekiel a sentinel, a watchman responsible for warning others of danger. Anyone who has felt responsible for another person's wellbeing knows the weight of it: the parent, the caregiver, the friend who sees trouble coming, and any of us tired of watching the world get used to things we never agreed to. But, God interrupts Ezekiel's assignment with something that sounds almost like heartbreak: "I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked… turn back, turn back." The responsibility God gave Ezekiel was never a cold demand. It flowed from a God who does not want to lose anyone, and who carries the weight with us.
Readings: Ezekiel 33:7-11; Psalm 119:33-40; Romans 13:8-14; Matthew 18:15-20.
Watch the full worship service: https://www.firstbaptistdc.org/listen-to-sermons/2026/9/3/sunday-sep-6-2026-still-here-when-its-too-much
Sunday, September 6, 2026 · The First Baptist Church of the City of Washington, D.C.

item.title: Still Here When You’re Burned Out
item.itunes:title: Still Here When You’re Burned Out
item.itunes:author: Eric Mathis
item.description:
"Still Here: When Holding On is Holy Enough" is a sermon series from Pastor Eric, a four-week journey through the Hebrew Bible with people who had reached the end of themselves. Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Joseph, and Jonah. These are not tidy people, and Scripture does not look away from them. In fact, it hands them the microphone. The series does not promise that everything is fine. It promises something better and harder—that holding on, barely and by a thread, turns out to be holy enough, because we are not the ones finally doing the holding.
In this first message of the series, Pastor Eric preaches on Jeremiah, who found himself where many people actually live: doing the faithful thing and quietly wondering if it is worth it. Jeremiah makes one of the most raw complaints in all of Scripture, and God does not strike him down for it. Honesty with God, it turns out, is not the opposite of faith. It may be its deepest form.
Readings: Jeremiah 15:15-21; Romans 12:9-21; Matthew 16:21-28.
Watch the full worship service: https://www.firstbaptistdc.org/listen-to-sermons/2026/8/26/sunday-aug-30-2026-still-here-when-youre-burned-out

item.title: Say It with Your Life
item.itunes:title: Say It with Your Life
item.itunes:author: Julie Pennington-Russell
item.description:
Pastor Julie turns to Matthew 16:13-20, where Jesus puts the question to Peter: "Who do you say that I am?" Peter answers correctly—only to discover that saying the words is just the beginning. A confession like this one isn't something you recite…it's something you live.
With "Say It with Your Life," Pastor Julie brings the summer series Tell Us a Story to a close.
Readings: Psalm 124; Romans 12:1-8; Matthew 16:13-20.

item.title: Crumbs and Categories
item.itunes:title: Crumbs and Categories
item.itunes:author: Julie Pennington-Russell
item.description:
A Canaanite woman refuses to stop shouting for her daughter's life, even after Jesus tries to wave her off. Pastor Julie preaches the message, "Crumbs and Categories," from Matthew 15:21-28. She persists past the silence, past the dismissal, past every category that says she doesn't belong.
The sermon watches her change Jesus' mind, and asks what that says about who gets a place at the table.
Readings: Psalm 133; Romans 11:1-2a, 29-36; Matthew 15:21-28.

item.title: Little Faith, Big Water
item.itunes:title: Little Faith, Big Water
item.itunes:author: Julie Pennington-Russell
item.description:
Pastor Julie preaches the message "Little Faith, Big Water" from Matthew 14:22-33.
The disciples are alone on the sea, straining against the wind in the dark hours before dawn. The wind is against them. The waves are climbing into the boat when a figure appears walking toward them across the water. And then there's Peter, who starts to sink before he starts to believe.
This story reminds us that faith isn't the absence of fear or doubt. Sometimes it's simply reaching for the hand that is already reaching for us.
Readings: Matthew 14:22-33.

item.title: Hidden and Holy
item.itunes:title: Hidden and Holy
item.itunes:author: Julie Pennington-Russell
item.description:
Pastor Julie preaches on Matthew 13:31–33, 44–51.
A mustard seed. A pinch of yeast. A coin, a pearl, a net. The sermon turns to five small stories about the reign of God—and how it keeps showing up in the most ordinary places. In these brief parables, Jesus points to a kindom that grows quietly, hides in plain sight, and turns up where we least expect it. The sermon considers how the holy might be tucked into the ordinary corners of your own life.
Readings: Psalm 119:129-136; Romans 8:31-39; Matthew 13:31-33, 44-51.

item.title: What If I'm Mad at God?
item.itunes:title: What If I'm Mad at God?
item.itunes:author: Julie Pennington-Russell
item.description:
Honest, unvarnished, straight-from-the-gut prayer is everywhere in Scripture. Which raises a question worth sitting with: Why do so many of us think it's off-limits?
Moses didn't. In this text, he tells God he's done—overwhelmed, furious, ready to quit. It is not a polite prayer. And yet it's the prayer God answers.
Pastor Julie closes the Honest to God series with an invitation to stop editing yourself before you come to God. Bring the anger. Bring the exhaustion. Bring the prayer you've been too careful to say.
Sermon text: Numbers 11:1-15.
Readings: Numbers 11:1-15; Romans 6:1b-11; Matthew 27:32-46.
Watch the full worship service: https://www.firstbaptistdc.org/listen-to-sermons/2026/6/18/sunday-jun-21-2026-what-if-im-mad-at-god
